overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely respond to a December 19, 2018 complaint, declined to review the untimely review-sufficiency claim, and found no intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission did not properly review two earlier OML complaints at its December 20, 2018 meeting, deferring responses without substantive discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find this allegation untimely and decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to respond within the statutory time to the December 19, 2018 OML complaint, which was not answered until February 20, 2019.
allegations.key_passage: By not responding to the December 19 complaint until February 20, in the absence of an extension of time granted by this Office, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the failure to respond to the December 19 complaint was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence that the Commission intended not to respond to the December 19 complaint in particular, we decline to find an intentional violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
